originality.rationale: Helleloid et al. (arXiv:0804.1095) gives the rule, monotonicity and general diameter bounds, but its inspected text does not imply the labelled Heawood four-peg criterion, 434 irredundant five-sets, or 336/84/168 orbit counts. Beeler–Gray 2013 and Engbers–Stocker 2014 address a terminal-one-peg objective with initial all-but-one occupancy (the latter also permits reverse moves). Semantic published-finding corpus comparisons found similar Heawood topics under materially different move and quantifier rules. This is a best-knowledge originality judgement, not priority certification.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete finite classification in the smallest symmetric projective-plane incidence graph, not an arbitrary slice. Three concise incidence configurations recognize every optimal four-peg distribution, while 434 irredundant five-peg sets display nonuniform minimal resource needs. A Fano quadrangle/secant obstruction at five pegs and the sharp all-distributions eight-peg bound link sparse peg mobility to finite-geometric structure. These precise counts and geometric classes plausibly serve as a benchmark for projective-plane and graph-pegging generalizations, without claiming a paper-sized advance.
